message.content: Lions mate during the breeding season, which can occur year‑round but peaks in spring and summer. A male will approach a receptive female, often after establishing dominance through scent marking and vocalizations. If the female accepts, they engage in a brief courtship ritual—sniffing each other’s genital area, licking, and vocalizing. Once paired, the male may guard the female from rivals while she gives birth. Mating itself lasts only a few minutes, but males may stay with the pride to protect offspring and maintain their status.
